deep.reconstruction:
This page is a faint pencil draft. Page 9 repeats it almost word for word and is more legible, so the readings here are guided by page 9.

(1) Top left is a commutative square A <- A', B <- B'. The vertical arrows are p: A -> B and p': A' -> B'. This is the base-change setting: a square of small categories, to be tested for whether limits computed upstairs commute with pulling back along B' -> B.

(2) Next comes the special case where B' is the point b. The top-right line is very likely 'A fibrée' over B. The fibre A_b embeds into the comma category A_{/b}, whose objects are pairs (a, u: p(a) -> b).

(3) The displayed formula is lim_{A_{/b}} (F|A_{/b}) -> lim_{A_b} (F|A_b). Page 9 labels this arrow 'iso' and adds 'pour tout F sur A (ou sur A_{/b})'.

Why it holds: if p is a fibration, the inclusion i: A_b -> A_{/b} has a right adjoint r. It sends (a, u) to u^*a, a chosen cartesian pullback, since Hom_{A_{/b}}(i x, (a, u)) = Hom_{A_b}(x, u^*a). So for every y the comma category i|y has a terminal object (r y, counit). It is therefore nonempty and connected; in fact it is contractible. Hence i is an initial (coinitial) functor, and restriction along i preserves limits. This gives the stated isomorphism for covariant F with values in sets or any complete category. Since i|y is contractible, i is even homotopy-initial (aspherical in Grothendieck's sense).

Page 9 continues 'A_b ... ∫ dans Hot'. That points to the homotopical version: homotopy limits / integration over A_b in the homotopy category. The resulting statement is that comma squares along fibred functors are exact squares, the base-change property later axiomatised in Les Dérivateurs.

The page sits in the cote 116 notes on mapping cones. The previous page treats topoi Top(X_i) and inverse limits over pro-objects. The likely purpose is to compute direct images / limits fibrewise, as needed for cones and homotopy limits in a derivator-like framework.
errors: No real error is visible, but the statement depends on variance, and the page does not specify it. The argument above works for covariant F and limits over A_{/b} with p fibred.
If F is a presheaf, i.e. the limit is taken over (A_{/b})^op, the same isomorphism instead needs p to be cofibred (opfibred).
The page itself only writes 'A fibrée[?]', so whether the conventions are consistent cannot be checked from this draft.

ideas.what: For a fibred functor p: A -> B, the fibre inclusion A_b -> A_{/b} admits a right adjoint and is therefore (homotopy) initial. Hence the limit over A_{/b} equals the limit over the fibre A_b.
ideas.modern_name: Fibres of a Grothendieck (op)fibration are homotopy-initial/final in the comma category; Quillen Theorem A style base change; Kan extensions computed fibrewise
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA1 fibred categories), Quillen (1973, Higher algebraic K-theory I), Grothendieck again in Les Dérivateurs
ideas.where_published: Les Dérivateurs (exact squares; fibred/cofibred functors give exact squares); related remarks in Pursuing Stacks

ideas.what: A commutative square of small categories, considered for exactness, i.e. base change for (homotopy) limits.
ideas.modern_name: Exact squares / homotopy exact squares (Beck–Chevalley condition in a derivator)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a faint early draft of a standard fact: fibres of a fibration compute comma-category limits, i.e. comma squares along fibrations are exact. Grothendieck later developed this systematically in Les Dérivateurs. Nothing on the page goes beyond that.

The displayed formula is probably lim_{A_{/b}} (F|A_{/b}) -> lim_{A_b} (F|A_b), with the arrow labelled 'iso' as on p. 9.
